neet_che_u18_t03_1.working: The carbylamine (isocyanide) test is given only by primary amines. Aniline is the only primary amine among the options.

neet_che_u18_t03_2.working: A sulphonamide insoluble in aqueous KOH has no acidic N-H, so it comes from a secondary amine. N-methylethanamine is secondary. Tertiary amines do not react at all, and primary amines give alkali-soluble products.

neet_che_u18_t03_3.working: Aromatic primary amines undergo diazotisation at 273-278 K. Benzenediazonium chloride forms and is stable at this temperature, so no N2 is evolved.

neet_che_u18_t03_4.working: A: aliphatic 1° amine gives N2 effervescence (III). B: aniline at low temperature gives a diazonium salt (IV). C: 2° amine gives a yellow oily N-nitrosamine (I). D: N,N-dimethylaniline undergoes ring nitrosation to a green p-nitroso compound (II).

neet_che_u18_t03_5.working: A is true: the N-H of a 1° sulphonamide is acidic. B is false: 3° amines do not react. C is true: p-toluenesulphonyl chloride works in the Hinsberg test. D is true: aniline is a 1° amine. E is false: N-methylaniline is a 2° amine. So A, C and D are correct.
